newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX heating oil ends 1996 with sizzling rally.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX heating oil ends 1996 with sizzling rally.

text.p: NYMEX heating oil ended 1996 Tuesday with a sizzling rally on a short squeeze in the expiring January contract that sent crude and gasoline to a strong year-end finish as well.
"There had been a good chance for a pullback in heat in the short term, so a lot of shorts got caught on the wrong end in expiry," said Mike DeLuca, trader with Prudential Securities.
January heating oil settled 2.27 cents higher at 72.84 cents a gallon and January gasoline settled 1.06 cents a gallon up at 70.67 cents ahead of the refined product prompt month expiry.
February crude ended 55 cents up at $25.92 a barrel after making a contract high of $25.97.

"It's the tail wagging the dog," said a New York dealer, explaining crude prices tracked the heating oil rally. But, traders noted volume was thin in a session shortened to 1300 EST due to the New Year holiday.

Heating oil was positive by mid-session on strength in gas oil futures on London's IPE, pushed up by freezing weather in Europe. When there was no indication that heat would decisively weaken, dealers said the January expiry gave way to last minute short covering in the front month.

The National Weather Service's six to 10 day forecast called for above normal temperatures in the key heating oil market of the northeastern United States and had led to an increase of short positions in heating oil, dealers said.

More detailed forecasts Tuesday by private weather services said temperatures would be below normal in the Northeast this week before warming next week, adding strength to the heating oil rally, dealers said.
NYMEX will reopen for regular trading hours Thursday.
-- Harry Milling, New York Energy Desk, ((212-859-1761))
